evals.prompt: Research: how to build a pure macOS application fully in Rust, not Swift — for the macos-application roadmap item.
evals.expected_output: Topic folder research/pure-rust-macos-ui/ with vetted chapters (platform docs, reference-project clones read outside the repo), a conclusion-dense summary with trade-offs, and bidirectional links with roadmap/macos-application/. Commits into that item's existing roadmap/macos-application branch and pull request under the Tailrocks-Skill trailer — one item, one branch, one PR — rather than opening a second PR for the research.

evals.prompt: Research macos-application — what did we miss, what directions exist?
evals.expected_output: Item-outward sweep: questions derived from the item's gaps and Open research questions, two to four evidence-backed directions with trade-offs and no verdict, decision-type questions routed to the item's Open questions.

evals.prompt: Research whether we should build the desktop app at all.
evals.expected_output: Decline the decision: that answer lives with the user; offer to research the factual ground (effort, platform constraints, prior art) that would inform it.

evals.prompt: Research Rust GUI options again — we already have a research topic covering half of this.
evals.expected_output: Detect the overlapping topic in research/README.md and extend that folder with new chapters and a refreshed summary instead of creating a duplicate.

evals.prompt: The investigators returned their chapters — vet them and write the summary.
evals.expected_output: One fresh-context, read-only citation-checker per chapter, blind to investigator reasoning, opens every cited source and returns per-citation SUPPORTS/PARTIAL/CONTRADICTS/UNREACHABLE verdicts; the orchestrator fixes misattributions, drops the unverifiable, opens load-bearing citations itself as a sample, resolves contradictions from the disputed sources, and stamps Vetted only after verdicts and sample agree; inline vetting only when parallel agents are unavailable, said aloud.

evals.prompt: Research how signed macOS app updates should be shipped — this is standing knowledge, no roadmap item.
evals.expected_output: Standalone lane per the delivery git contract: branch research/<topic-slug> off the base, chapters and summary committed with the Tailrocks-Skill trailer, a draft PR opened; the base branch is never pushed directly. One subject in one lane — this is not a second lane for a roadmap item, and a later invocation that links the topic to an item keeps working whichever lane is still open.
